 Mandy Moore’s ex Ryan Adams engaged to woman 30 years younger than him: ‘I’ve never been happier’ 
 By 
 Vanessa Serna 
 Published 
 Nov. 17, 2026, 8:38 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 
 Mandy Moore’s ex-husband Ryan Adams may have found his “happy ever after” with songwriter Kate Farr.
 The former Whiskeytown musician, 52, and Farr, 22, got engaged in October after six months of dating, he told TMZ in an interview published Tuesday.
 “I’ve never been happier in my life,” Adams gushed. “Kate is the most fascinating, kindest nerd I’ve ever met. She’s my best friend, and I’ve never been happier. Here’s to love.”

 The couple met through mutual friends earlier this year, and Farr moved to Los Angeles to live with Adams.
 However, Farr and Adams are considering packing their bags and moving back to the Midwest to be closer to their families.
 Adams was previously married to Moore from 2009 to 2016.

 The actress has since opened up about alleged emotional abuse throughout their seven-year marriage, including in a 2019 interview with the New York Times, where six other women detailed Adams’ alleged abuse and sexual misconduct.
 “He would always tell me, ‘You’re not a real musician, because you don’t play an instrument,’” she said, adding that he allegedly blocked her “ability to make new connections in the industry during a very pivotal and potentially lucrative time — my entire mid-to-late 20s.” 
 In the article, Adams was also accused of using his power to take advantage of young women in the music industry, allegedly threatening to ruin their aspiring careers if he didn’t get his way.

 At the time, Adams responded to the allegations, telling the outlet that Moore’s claims were “completely inconsistent with his view of the relationship” and labeled the entire article as “inaccurate.” 
 Additionally, during a 2019 podcast episode of Marc Maron’s “WTF” podcast, Moore claimed she felt “untenable” and “unattainable” in her marriage to Adams.
 The “A Walk to Remember” star explained she felt as if she was “drowning” in her “co-dependent” relationship.
 8 
 Farr moved to Los Angeles to be with Adams (seen here in 2000). Getty Images 
 8 
 Moore and Adams (seen here in 2008) were previously wed from 2009 to 2016. GC Images 
 The following year, Adams addressed the allegations in an apology letter, stating that he was “still reeling from the ripples of devastating effects that my actions triggered.”
 “In my effort to be a better man, I have fought to get sober, but this time I’m doing it with professional help,” he wrote. “Sobriety is a priority in my life, and so is my mental health. These, as I’m learning, go hand in hand.”
 Adams acknowledged that he has “mistreated people throughout my life and career,” adding, “All I can say is that I’m sorry. It’s that simple. This period of isolation and reflection made me realize that I needed to make significant changes in my life.”
